answer.rationale: Rollback is prohibited by compliance. Regional failover (memory_b2) helped with a latency degradation but does not address write-path saturation at settlement peak. Circuit breakers (memory_b4) protect against a dependency outage, not against capacity-driven latency on our own write path. Routing reads to replicas (memory_b5) would not relieve write-path p99. memory_b3 is the closest analogue: provisioning headroom ahead of heavy write load kept queue depth flat during a promotional surge. Here the surge is already present and the write path is saturated, so adding capacity is the one intervention that increases write throughput without dropping in-flight transactions and without touching the security-patched release. Scaling write-path nodes should bring p99 back toward target while preserving every customer write through the peak settlement window.
